what_happened: Research found that Mode B's refusal-time hook point (task-lock.sh queue-check || exit 1) lives only in commands/orchestrate.md, which is absent from this task's declared file_scope (only skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md is listed). Recorded as a finding/recommendation in the research report rather than left for mid-implementation discovery; plan phase should widen file_scope by this one entry before implementation.

class: reuse-not-reimplement confirmed by direct source read
what_happened: Confirmed directly in orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's own header comments that its collision comparison set already excludes any dependencies[]-edge-connected pair in either direction (A1 note) -- this means the dispatch's EDGE-PROPOSING STEP requires no new admission logic at all: add the edge via update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add, then re-probe the real script. Saves the implementation phase from having to discover or re-derive this mechanism empirically.

Research-flagged file_scope gap (commands/orchestrate.md, the only queue-check call site, absent from the declared four-entry file_scope) was resolved mechanically at plan time rather than mid-implementation: listing every touched file in the phases' 'Files to modify' blocks makes plan-file-scope-harvest.sh widen file_scope from 4 to 10 entries at plan postflight, the one moment --file-scope-add is admissible. Verified by running the harvester over the finished plan (10/10 paths harvested).

The EDGE-PROPOSING STEP's 'PROPOSE the serializing edge via update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add' admits two readings: emit the command, or perform the write (the latter being the only way the acceptance criterion's re-probe can show admit). Resolved in-plan as Decision 2 rather than escalated to the user: propose-only by default (conclusion time is the wrong moment to mutate state.json dependency edges unasked), with an opt-in --write-edges flag that writes then re-probes, and the acceptance demonstration run under --write-edges against a scratch tree.

Proved the selection doctrine's width-vs-chain nuance is vacuous within a ready-only candidate pool: a ready task's dependencies[] entries can never themselves be ready-pool members, since a predecessor must be status=completed (terminal, hence excluded from readiness). Simplified select_candidates() accordingly and documented the proof inline instead of implementing dead code.
